notes: Check weather conditions before visiting. Thunderstorms are common. Altitude range from 350’ to 8,182 feet. Sleep sloop S curves. Follow signs. Bring water. Expect Wildlife encounters.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
notes: Park hours are typically sunrise to sunset and closed on holidays. Check the NPS website or call ahead. There are some lookout points along the river bluff that are a higher elevation.

name: El Malpais National Monument
notes: Location is the Ranger Station for the NPS El Malpais Visitor Center.

name: El Morro National Monument
notes: Check weather. Two species of rattlesnakes live at El Morro. Never place your hands or feet where you cannot see. Rattlesnakes or black widow spiders may be sheltered there. Cellular service spotty.

name: Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument
notes: Florissant Fossil Beds National Monument is stop 23 on the Pikes Peak Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/pikes-peak

name: Fort Union National Monument
notes: thunderstorms and severe lightning can be powerful and sudden. Eat plenty of food and drink at least one gallon of water each day. Carry and drink water during all activities, Cell service spotty.

name: George Washington Carver National Monument
notes: There are no fees to access this park, but the parking lot is very large. Visitor center is an interesting tour if you activate during open hours. The gate is generally open round-the-clock, but that may change.

name: Gila Cliff Dwellings National Monument
notes: This is a Pack-It-In, Pack-It-Out area. There is no food or drink (other than water) allowed on the trail or in the dwellings. There are picnic tables at the Gila Visitor Center,

name: Homestead National Historical Park
notes: High noise levels reported recently at this park, especially at the eastern visitor center.

name: Little Bighorn Battlefield National Monument
notes: No dogs allowed outside of vehicles.

name: Petroglyph National Monument
notes: Eat before you visit and drink a least one gallon of water each day. Storms and flash floods can be powerful and sudden. When lightning is present, return to your vehicle as soon as possible. Never try to cross a wash of running water.

name: Salinas Pueblo Missions, Gran Quivira Unit, National Monument
notes: Cellular spotty. Check weather conditions before visiting. The elevation at our 3 sites is above 6,000 feet and can cause breathing difficulties for some people

name: White Sands National Park
notes: Park operating hours vary by season, and is occasionally closed for periods of time due to missile tests on the adjacent White Sands Missile Range. Visitors are encouraged to check Park Closure webpage to verify that a closure is not in effect.

name: Sid Simpson State Park
notes: It was a state park that was donated to Quincy Park District now named Bob Bangert Park

name: Arkansas Museum of Natural Resources State Park
notes: This state park offers a good parking area and cell coverage. Best operated from your automible.

name: Bull Shoals White River State Park
notes: Full service camp ground with all you would expect from a state park.

name: Conway Cemetery State Park
notes: This is a very small park. There are no facilities on this location. Good parking lot to set up in.

name: Crowley's Ridge State Park
notes: Campsites, cabins, pavillion and picnic areas along with trails make a good activation.

name: Daisy State Park
notes: This is a nice state park with plenty of places to activate from.

name: Davidsonville Historic (Old) State Park
notes: Campsites and tables are available along with several trails.

name: DeGray Lake Resort State Park
notes: Great park to activate. Camping, lodge, picnic they are all here.

name: Delta Heritage Trails State Park
notes: There are 44 miles so far of trails in this park. Check the website https://www.arkansasstateparks.com/parks/delta-heritage-trail-state-park)

name: Devil's Den State Park
notes: No cell service unless you go up the mountain. Parking at the sign on the west side of the park you will have service. This is a nice park with full service. During the summer you can sometimes get food.

name: Herman Davis State Park
notes: This is a very small state park with a small parking area. One can activate from the grassy area/lawn. There are a couple of benches to sit on.This historic site is in Manila at the corner of Ark. 18 and Baltimore Street.

name: Hobbs State Park
notes: Hike and bike in campsites are availavle for activation along with the parking log at the visitors center. There is a large pavilion that may be used for activation.

name: Jacksonport State Park
notes: The state park offers good activation areas such as picnic tables parking areas and camping spots.

name: Jenkins Ferry State Park
notes: Picnic area and you can also activate it from your car.

name: Lake Catherine State Park
notes: As with most state parks there are lots of places to activate. Picnic tables or parking lots. This is a nice state park.

name: Lake Charles State Park
notes: Camping and picnic tables along with a pavilion and trails make an activation possible.

name: Lake Chicot State Park
notes: Camping, and picnic area are all good places to set up. There may be LOTS of insects depending on time of the year so be prepared.

name: Lake Dardanelle State Park
notes: Plenty of places to activate from here in this park. Tables and campsites .

name: Lake Fort Smith State Park
notes: What you would expect from a full service park. This is also a 3 park activation. K-10508, K-4425 and K-1092 the State Park. You have to activate near the trail

name: Lake Frierson State Park
notes: The park is 10 miles north of Jonesboro on Hwy. 141.Nearby are picnic sites, a pavilion, and a hiking trail for activations. There are 7 campsites.

name: Lake Ouachita State Park
notes: A good park to activate. Plenty of places and tables.

name: Logoly State Park
notes: Good access to this park. Several places that are good to activate.

name: Lower White River Museum State Park
notes: This is a small park. There is a parking lot to activate from. It is in the middle of the town.

name: Mammoth Spring State Park
notes: Picnic area and a walking trail along with the parking log for activation

name: Millwood State Park
notes: A good state park with many areas to set up and activate.

name: Mississippi River State Park
notes: Campground picnic area and parking areas make this a good activation area.

name: Moro Bay State Park
notes: Easy access to this state park.

name: Mount Nebo State Park
notes: This state park sits on top of a 3/4 long flat top mountain. Realy great scenery of the Arkansas River Valley. There is a large parking lot on the West end of the mountain where you can watch the sun go down. You can activate it from your car here or ta

name: Historic Washington State Park
notes: This is an interesting historic park. The confluence of 4 trails makes it a busy POTA activation. Trail of Tears, Southwest Trail, The Civil War Trail, and The Camden Expedition Scenic Highway and Scenic Byway. The park staff here are awesome to activa

name: Petit Jean State Park
notes: Many places to activate this park from. It has many scenic vistas. The airport is part of the park.

name: Pinnacle Mountain State Park
notes: Lots of places to set up around picnic tables or from your car.

name: Poison Springs Battleground State Park
notes: This park has no visitor center but there are tables or you can activate from your car. Good cell service.

name: Powhatan State Park
notes: Powhatan Arkansas at highway 25. There are picnic tables that overlook the Black River from what the ranger tells me. Along with the parking area for activations.

name: Prairie Grove Battlefield State Park
notes: There are a couple of pavilions that you have to contact the park to use. A driving trail through the park will yield a couple of large parking area and a couple of pull offs. Picnic tables are also available.

name: Queen Wilhelmina State Park
notes: This state park sits atop a mountain. All amities are here along with a hamfest in September. Great activation site. Probably can get some 2m contacts from the park.

name: South Arkansas Arboretum State Park
notes: This is a 13-acre state park. Good Parking area.

name: Plumb Bayou Mounds Archeological State Park
notes: Parking lot and a few picnic tables for an activation.

name: White Oak Lake State Park
notes: The friendly staff at this park is always helpful . It is also part of K-9162, K-9681 and K-7435.

name: Withrow Springs State Park
notes: This is a nice state park with camping and a picnic area. Maybe you can get cell signal.

name: Arkansas River Headwaters Recreation Park
notes: The Arkansas River Headwaters Recreation Area is managed jointly by CPW, BLM https://www.blm.gov/visit/arkansas-headwaters-recreation-area, and USFS. It follows the Arkansas River for about 150 miles and has 150 distinct river access points.

name: Cheyenne Mountain State Park
notes: NOTE: Stargate Command is not within the boundaries of this park.

name: Highline Lake State Park
notes: This park is stop 12 on the Grand Valley Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/western-colorado/grand-valley.

name: James M. Robb - Colorado River State Park
notes: This park is comprised of 5 separate sections, known as the "string of pearls." It is on the Grand Valley Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/western-colorado/grand-valley

name: Lake Pueblo State Park
notes: Lake Pueblo State Park is stop 5 on the Whitewater Colorado Birding Trail. https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/whitewater/

name: Paonia State Park
notes: This park is dtop 14 on the Fruitgrowers Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/western-colorado/fruitgrowers.

name: San Luis Lakes State Wildlife Area
Spinney Mountain State Park
notes: Spinney is stop 8 on the South Park Birding Trail https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/south-park.

name: Sylvan Lake State Park
notes: This park is stop 12 on the Eagle Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/eagle.

name: Yampa River State Park
notes: A 134-mile stretch of the Yampa River is the heart of Yampa River State Park. It has 13 access point sites stretching from Hayden to the Dinosaur National Monument near the Utah border.

name: Dawkins Line Rail Trail State Park
Fishtrap Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Although owned by US Army Corps of Engineers since 2016, Fishtrap Lake became a Kentucky State Park in 2003 until its transfer of ownership, therefore it shall remain part of the POTA system.

name: Levi Jackson Wilderness Road State Park
notes: This is a former State park that became a city park. When parks are "demoted" like this, they may remain a POTA park, as long as they were a POTA park when they were a State Park.

name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park
Taylorsville Lake State Park
notes: Park is open all year. Campground is normally closed mid November thru mid March each year.

name: Blue Licks Battlefield State Park
notes: Setup can be lower parking lot along River Road, or parking area on pool road, or opposite side of US-68 on Heritage Trail. Please DO NOT setup on the Battlefield area.

name: Carter Caves State Park
notes: https://fivco.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Carter-Caves-State-Resort-Park-Topographic-Trails-Map.pdf GIS map for more boundary info: https://opengisdata.ky.gov/datasets/kygeonet::state-park-boundaries-1/explore?location=38.372463%2C-83.120632%2C13.72

name: Dale Hollow State Park
notes: The above coordinates are to a large parking area away from the resort which may have high noise floor.

name: General Butler State Park
notes: Please call ahead about a Special Use Permit

name: Lake Cumberland State Park
notes: The above coordinates are to the State Resort Park lodge, but if lodge area creates too much noise, the following coordinates are to a pull-off along resort park roadway 36.912554,-85.049013

name: Amnicon Falls State Park
notes: A vehicle pass is required. Park hours are 6am-11pm. Amnicon Falls State Park features a series of delightful waterfalls and rapids along the Amnicon River. See website for more details.

name: Aztalan State Park
notes: Vehicle pass required. Hours are 6am-11pm. Aztalan State Park is a National Historic Landmark and contains one of Wisconsin's most important archaeological sites, showcasing an ancient Middle-Mississippian village that thrived between A.D. 1000 and 1300.

name: Belmont Mound State Park
notes: Vehicle pass is NOT required at this park. Park hours 6am-11pm. The top of Belmont Mound is 1,400 feet above sea level, providing some fantastic views of the area. See website for more details.

name: Big Bay State Park
notes: Park is on an island. Car ferry access available. Ice road can also be used in winter if conditions allow. Park hours 6am-11pm. Big Bay SP features picturesque sandstone bluffs along 4 miles of Lake Superior shoreline. See website for more details.

name: Big Foot Beach State Park
notes: A vehicle pass is required for this park. Hours are 6am-11pm. Located on the shores of Lake Geneva, Big Foot Beach State Park offers 5 miles of hiking trails, a family campground, swimming beach and picnic and playground areas.

name: Blue Mound State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Perched atop the highest point in southern Wisconsin, Blue Mound State Park offers spectacular views and unique geological features. See website for more details.

name: Brunet Island State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Brunet Island State Park, on the Chippewa and Fisher rivers, offers more than 1,300 acres of scenic beauty and recreational opportunities. See website for more details.

name: Buckhorn State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Buckhorn State Park is a paradise for water enthusiasts, hunters, hikers, campers and nature lovers. See website for more details.

name: Campbellsport Drumlin State Park
notes: Small State Park located in Fond Du Lac County. No parking is available other than roadside shoulder parking. Best spot would be on the west side of Sunset Dr at the top of the hill. Walk in activations are also possible.

name: Copper Culture State Park
notes: Copper Culture State Park was the site of a prehistoric cemetery of the Old Copper Complex people who occupied the northern Midwest from ca. 4000 – 2000 BC. Park has been grandfathered into POTA. See website for additional details.

name: Copper Falls State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Ancient lava flows, deep gorges and spectacular waterfalls make Copper Falls State Park one of Wisconsin's most scenic parks. See website for more details.

name: Council Grounds State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Located along the beautiful Wisconsin River near the site of Native American encampments, Council Grounds State Park is a favorite for water enthusiasts. See website for more details.

name: Cross Plains State Park
notes: Vehicle pass NOT required for this park. Parking is available outside of the park. Parking lot south of Old Salk Pass Rd is outside of the park and not a valid location for this park. A short walk up the Ice Age Trail will have you on the property.

name: Devil's Lake State Park
notes: Wisconsin vehicle admission pass or National Park pass required. Park open 6am-11pm. Devil's Lake State Park offers magnificent views from 500-foot quartzite bluffs overlooking a 360-acre lake. See website for more info.

name: Grand Traverse Island State Park
notes: This is a tiny park on Detroit Island. There are a few different parcels of land that are the State Park. Door County GIS maps shows land is owned by the Wisconsin DNR. Map is also available and searchable on Google.

name: Governor Dodge State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Governor Dodge State Park is one of the state's largest parks, with over 5,000 acres of steep hills, bluffs and deep valleys plus two lakes and a waterfall. See website for more details.

name: Governor Nelson State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Located on 10,000-acre Lake Mendota, recreation and nature mingle within sight of the State Capitol. See website for more details.

name: Governor Thompson State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. More than 2,800 acres of woods, a family campground, picnic and beach area on Woods Lake, hiking and skiing trails, and 6 miles of shoreline on Caldron Falls Flowage. See website for more details.

name: Harrington Beach State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Harrington Beach State Park has more than a mile of beach along Lake Michigan. See website for more details.

name: Hartman Creek State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Located on the beautiful Chain O' Lakes, Hartman Creek State Park is a quiet and friendly, natural gem and a popular destination in central Wisconsin. See website for more details.

name: High Cliff State Park
notes: High Cliff State Park is the only state-owned recreational area on Lake Winnebago, Wisconsin's largest lake. Vehicle pass required for this park. Park is open from 6am-11pm.

name: Kinnickinnic State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Located where the St. Croix and Kinnickinnic rivers meet. See website for more details.

name: Kohler-Andrae State Park
notes: Park hours 6am-11pm. Kohler-Andrae is the home of majestic sand dunes, miles of golden beach, shimmering blue Lake Michigan water. Vehicle pass required for this park.

name: Lake Kegonsa State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Lake Kegonsa State Park offers a variety of recreational activities set along a 3,200-acre lake. See website for more details.

name: Lake Wissota State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Lake Wissota State Park, northeast of Chippewa Falls, offers secluded campsites, hiking, biking and horseback riding trails, picnic and playground areas and a swimming beach on a 6,300-acre man-made lake.

name: Lakeshore State Park
notes: This is an in-city park. Vehicle pass is not required. Hours are 6am-10pm. The Hank Aaron State Trail K-9800 runs thru parts of this park as well.

name: Merrick State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Merrick State Park is located on the beautiful backwaters of the Mississippi River. See website for more details.

name: Mill Bluff State Park
notes: Wisconsin vehicle admission pass or National Park pass required. Park open 6am-11pm. Part of the Ice Age National Scientific Reserve, Mill Bluff State Park offers a spectacular view of picturesque rock formations. See website for more details.

name: Mirror Lake State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Mirror Lake State Park is named for its centerpiece, a lake which often is so calm that not a ripple marks its surface. See website for more details.

name: Natural Bridge State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Natural Bridge State Park has a natural sandstone arch created by the eroding effects of wind and water. The bridge opening is 25 feet high by 35 feet wide. See website for additional details.

name: Nelson Dewey State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Nelson Dewey State Park overlooks the Mississippi River from a 500-foot bluff. See website for more details.

name: New Glarus Woods State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. New Glarus Woods State Park is a 435-acre state park offering camping, hiking, picnicking and snowshoeing just south of the city of New Glarus. Be sure to grab a Spotted Cow while in the area.

name: Newport State Park
notes: Vehicle pass required for this park. Park hours 6am-11pm. Newport's offers over 2,300 acres of forest on 11 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline, 30 miles of hiking trails, and backpack camping as a quiet alternative to bustling Door County.

name: Pattison State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Pattison State Park features the highest waterfalls in Wisconsin and the fourth highest waterfall east of the Rocky Mountains. Big Manitou Falls is 165 feet high and Twin Little Manitou Falls is 31 feet high.

name: Peninsula State Park
notes: Vehicle pass required for this park. Park hours 6am-11pm. Peninsula State Park offers over 460 campsites, three group camps, a summer theater, an 18-hole golf course, sand beach, bike trails, a lighthouse and eight miles of Door County shoreline.

name: Perrot State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Perrot State Park's 1,200 acres are nestled among 500-foot bluffs where the Trempealeau and Mississippi rivers meet. See website for more details.

name: Potawatomi State Park
notes: Vehicle pass required. Hours are 6am-11pm. Potawatomi State Park on the shore of Sturgeon Bay in southern Door County, has 1,200 acres of gently rolling upland terrain bordered by steep slopes and rugged limestone cliffs.

name: Rib Mountain State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. This billion-year-old hill is one of the oldest geological formations on Earth. See website for more details.

name: Roche-A-Cri State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Roche-A-Cri State Park, established in 1948, protects a 300-foot-high rock outcropping and Native American petroglyphs and pictographs. See website for more details.

name: Rock Island State Park
notes: This is an island park accessible by ferry. No vehicles allowed on the island, so activations on foot/portable only. No vehicle pass required.

name: Rocky Arbor State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. The rock forming Rocky Arbor's gorge is sandstone that geologists have aged at about 500 million years. See website for more details.

name: Straight Lake State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Lake views and glacial features provide great vistas on the trails within this 2,000-acre park. See website for more details.

name: Tower Hill State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Former lead mining and ammo manufacturing area. By the 1840s, southwest Wisconsin mines were producing more than half of the nation's lead. See website for more details. See website for more details.

name: Whitefish Dunes State Park
notes: Vehicle pass required. Hours are 6am-8pm. Whitefish Dunes State Park protects the fragile dune environment on the eastern Door County Peninsula.

name: Wildcat Mountain State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. Located on a ridge rising steeply above the Kickapoo River. See website for more details.

name: Willow River State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. 2,800 acres of park offering views of Willow Falls and the Willow River Gorge. See website for more details.

name: Wyalusing State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. One of Wisconsin's oldest state parks. See website for more details.

name: Yellowstone Lake State Park
notes: Vehicle sticker required. Park open 6am-11pm. One of a few lakes in southwestern Wisconsin, 450-acre Yellowstone Lake State Park is a popular year-round recreation area. See website for more details.

name: Babler Memorial State Park
notes: Full service State Park that can be busy at peak times. Will find yourself driving some time around the roads to find a suitable spot to activate, and settle on an unoccupied campsite or group area.

name: Sam A. Baker State Park
notes: Full service park with many usual facilities, plus equestrian. Picnic, shelters, etc.

name: Bennett Spring State Park
notes: This park is focused on camping and fishing. Generally very busy. Several parking lots, some open spaces, but be aware of foot traffic. Nice restaurant on site, fish hatchery fishing with special permit.

name: Big Lake State Park
notes: Was heavily damaged by flooding but re-opened as a day use only park. Lots of parking lots, open areas, picnic tables, etc. Friendly rangers.

name: Big Oak Tree State Park
notes: Smaller limited services State Park. Noted for hiking trails, shelters, and picnic areas.

name: Big Sugar Creek State Park
notes: Smaller park with hiking trails. This park is remote and the road crosses streams that may be over the bridges and the road can be washed out. Use caution.

name: Castlewood State Park
notes: This park is close to town and can be very busy at peak times. Very busy. Hiking and biking trails, open areas, limited parking.

name: Crowder State Park
notes: Easy to find...primarily a campground park with boating and fishing access. Several parking lots and open areas to activate.

name: Cuivre River State Park
notes: This park gives the impression that it has seen better days, but activation spots are easy to find. Scenic areas are available, as is some fishing.

name: Current River State Park
notes: Smaller historic park with hiking trails and picnic sites.

name: Don Robinson State Park
notes: Primarily a hiking and picnic park. Limited parking areas and limited open areas.

name: Echo Bluff State Park
notes: This is a large full-service State Park that offers year-round activities and accommodation. Offers a lodge.

name: Elephant Rocks State Park
notes: Smaller geologic themed park with hiking trails, picnic areas, and trails designed for people with visual and physical disabilities.

name: Finger Lakes State Park
notes: Full-featured State Park. Several parking lots and various venues for activations. Close to Columbia, so can be busy at peak times.

name: Graham Cave State Park
notes: Nice park, but with widely varying elevations. Parking lot near the ranger station is best, and the rangers are very friendly.

name: Grand Gulf State Park
notes: Primarily a hike and sight-seeing park. Some picnic and open areas, with limited parking.

name: Ha Ha Tonka State Park
notes: Popular day park with many facilities. Several parking lots, open areas, shorelines, shelters, etc. Widely varying elevations around the park.

name: Harry S Truman State Park
notes: Very popular State Park, lots of facilities, but can be very busy at peak times. Also subject to flooding.

name: Hawn State Park
notes: Larger park with very good hiking trails and campground.

name: Johnson's Shut-Ins State Park
notes: Textbook State Park...nice picnic areas, hiking trails, things to see, unusual sights, etc. Hiking trails include the Ozark State Trail that can take you into the ONLY access to Jay Nixon State Park and further east across the State.

name: Jones-Confluence Point State Park
notes: Primarily and hiking and bird-watching park. Limited parking.

name: Katy Trail State Park
notes: This is a "trail park" built on an old railroad bed. There are several "depots" along the trail, so activation is possible from one of the depots or spurs, or from the trail itself, as long as antenna doesn't block trail.

name: Knob Noster State Park
notes: Typical park, parking lots, picnic areas, etc. Some limited shelter space. Terrain elevation varies.

name: Lake of the Ozarks State Park
notes: Large premium State Park. Almost every facility available. The Lee C Fine Airport is in the park (if you step off the apron). Many parking lots, hiking trails, some open spaces, especially along the trails.

name: Lake Wappapello State Park
notes: Larger full-service State Park with all possible activities plus equestrian trails/facilities. Large lake and boating.

name: Lewis and Clark State Park
notes: Small State Park that was devastated during recent floods. Check with the park office for real-time status before before driving out during the spring season. There are several parking lots and a few shelters, park benches.

name: Long Branch State Park
notes: Open areas abound, causeway across the lake. Borders K-5697 (separated by a road) at the north end of the lake.

name: Mark Twain State Park
notes: Typical State with camping, fishing, etc. Several parking lots and open spaces to activate.

name: Meramec State Park
notes: Full service State Park with camping, picnic areas, cabins and a motel.

name: Montauk State Park
notes: Full service park with rooms and cabins with a dining lodge offered for overnight stays.

name: Morris State Park
notes: Primarily a hiking State Park...smaller park with few facilities.

name: Onondaga Cave State Park
notes: Scenic park, picnic areas, parking lots and limited open areas.

name: Pershing State Park
notes: Typical state park...variety of facilities and open spaces or picnic areas. Limited shelters. Easy to find.

name: Pomme de Terre State Park
notes: This is primarily a campground State Park. Oddly very few open areas, parking lots or picnic areas. Several trails around the lake to activate from shorelines or bluffs.

name: Prairie State Park
notes: This is a very open park...and there are roaming bison everywhere. There is a small parking lot on a slight rise on the access road that is the best activating spot, but other spots are available for different setups.

name: Roaring River State Park
notes: This park is in a deep east-west valley between two ridges (open to the east), but activating on both 20 and 40 meters was easy. Several camping, picnic, parking spots available.

name: Robertsville State Park
notes: Campgrounds and picnic areas with some open areas and limited parking at peak times.

name: Rock Bridge Memorial State Park
notes: Typical small State park...several open spaces, picnic areas, limited shelters, walking paths. Popular with dog-walkers so be mindful of walkways.

name: Route 66 State Park
notes: Somewhat of a small park compressed into a highway/commercial area. By far the best activating location is the large, paved boat launch area on the south east end.

name: St. Francois State Park
notes: Larger full service State Park.

name: St. Joe State Park
notes: Many facilities at this park, camping, picnic, equestrian, hiking, fishing, etc. Also an Off-road-Vehicle trail that requires a day permit ranging fro $5 to $10 depending on type of vehicle.

name: Stockton State Park
notes: Nice State Park with many facilities. Note that there are many Corps of Engineers sites around the park/lake that are NOT in K-1786. The islands in the lake are part of the US Islands program.

name: Table Rock State Park
notes: Very scenic park, but be aware that the area has numerous tourist scenic overlooks that are not in the park. Several parking lots, some shelters. Generally a very busy park next door to Branson.

name: Taum Sauk Mountain State Park
notes: The park has a 12-site basic campground, a special-use area for group camping, and a picnic area. This park also includes SOTA sites inside and nearby.

name: Thousand Hills State Park
notes: Full service State Park, but with several parking lots, and picnic areas.

name: Trail of Tears State Park
notes: Nice park, especially nice scenic views of the river from overlooks. Hiking trails, picnic areas, etc.

name: Van Meter State Park
notes: This is primarily a campground park with very large mature trees. Limited parking/picnic areas, almost no open spaces, so antennas will be under trees, although not reportedly been a problem to activate.

name: Wakonda State Park
notes: Full-featured State Park, but not very large. A main parking lot with a few smaller ones and several hiking trails. Fishing is good. Not much day use, so the rangers may be puzzled at just wanting to stay for an hour, but they are friendly.

name: Wallace State Park
notes: Typical park, lots of parking lots, some open spaces. Terrain elevation varies. Campgrounds and limited shelters may be available.

name: Washington State Park
notes: Full-service smaller State Park...no special issues.

name: Watkins Mill State Park
notes: Nice lakeshore park. A walking trail can be activated on foot. Several picnic tables lakeshore, and a larger shelter that isn't usually occupied weekdays.

name: Weston Bend State Park

name: Arrow Rock State Historic Site

name: Confederate Memorial State Historic Site

name: Dillard Mill State Historic Site

name: Felix Vallé House State Historic Site

name: First Missouri State Capitol State Historic Site

name: Gov. Daniel Dunklin's Grave State Historic Site

name: Hunter-Dawson State Historic Site

name: Mastodon State Historic Site

name: Missouri Mines State Historic Site

name: Sandy Creek Covered Bridge State Historic Site

name: Towosahgy State Historic Site

name: Union Covered Bridge State Historic Site

name: Eleven Point State Park

name: Nebraska National Forest

name: Chimney Rock National Historic Site

name: Mines of Spain State Recreation Area

name: Arapaho National Forest
notes: Jointly managed with the Roosevelt National Forest and the Pawnee National Grasslands. The varied terrain and vast acreage offers a wide variety of options for operators.

name: Grand Mesa National Forest
notes: The Grand Mesa National Forest offers a wide variety of terrain and wide expanses which present a variety of challenges to radio operators.

name: Rio Grande National Forest
notes: The Rio Grande NF offers a variety of terrain and challenges. Activation can be from an improved campground or from the backcountry.

name: San Isabel National Forest
notes: The San Isabel National Forest offers a wide variety of terrain and can present an adventure or an easy outing, depending on the skills and desires of the activator.

name: Uncompahgre National Forest
notes: The Uncompahgre NF provides a wide variety of terrain with a number of challenging places from which to activate.

name: Browns Canyon National Monument
notes: Activities include hiking, backpacking, camping, horseback riding, snowshoeing, and photography.

name: Canyons of the Ancients National Monument
John Henry Kirby Memorial State Forest
Ozark-St. Francis National Forest
notes: Large area to operate from. Many places you can setup the problem may be choosing one. It also covers a couple of other parks.

name: Poison Springs State Forest
notes: This area has some primitive camping, a horse trail and a couple of dirt access roads. It can be activated by car. It can also be activated at the Poison Springs State Park as it is inside the State Forest.

name: Caribou-Targhee National Forest
notes: Best access May thru October

name: Daniel Boone National Forest
notes: Large forest, many locations and tracts with varied attractions.

name: Mark Twain National Forest
notes: This forest is very large and has several discontinuous tracts spanning almost the entire state. Research before activating. Large variety of accesses, lots, waterways, etc.

name: Custer Gallatin National Forest
notes: This listing reflects the combining of Custer and Gallatin National Forests. K-4503, the old Gallatin NF listing, has been archived and can no longer be activated. Activations and contacts from old listing remain in your account. K0HAA

name: Helena - Lewis and Clark National Forest
notes: This listing reflects the combining of Helena and Lewis and Clark National Forests. K-4572, the old Lewis and Clark NF listing, has been archived and can no longer be activated. Activations and contacts from old listing remain in your account. K0HAA

name: Carson National Forest
notes: The Carson National Forest covers 1.5 million acres and is located in beautiful Northern New Mexico. Elevations rise from 6,000 feet to 13,161 feet at Wheeler Peak, the highest point in New Mexico.

name: Cibola National Forest
notes: Elevation: 2,000'-11,301'. Located in New Mexico, western Texas and western Oklahoma.

name: Lincoln National Forest
notes: Elevations range from 4,000 to 11,500 feet

name: Santa Fe National Forest
notes: The Santa Fe National Forest is very large with numerous places to activate. The pin location is just one. Excellent site for forest boundaries, https://www.fs.usda.gov/ivm/

name: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest

name: Harry S. Truman Birthplace State Historic Site
notes: An in-town park with very little open area. Best to activate from mobile. Not many options.

name: World War I Museum National Memorial
notes: The front lawn area has many picnic tables and trees. Weekends often have special events that occupy the entire lawn. Otherwise, this park has been activated numerous times. Some rangers/docents are hams/friendly.

name: Barkley Memorial State Forest
notes: Many 3rd party websites list this as a "state park". At best it is an abandoned public property that has received a "Barkley State Forest Parking Lot" sign. At dead end of a road, with some private property in vicinity.

name: Gifford State Forest
notes: DNR forester confirms Gifford is OPEN. Some tourist websites incorrectly report that it is closed. No in boundary parking, hike-in park activation only. No trails or clearings available - so be prepared.

name: Holst State Forest
notes: The forest begins at the end of a muddy 1/2 mile dirt road. Parking for maybe two vehicles at a trail head into the forest.

name: Loess Hills State Forest
notes: This forest has several tracts separated by several miles. Conveniently, the access to both the Preparation Canyon State Park and this forest is at a fork in the road.

name: Pilot Mound State Forest
notes: Small SF within Boone and Yellow forests. Must do homework before finding this one.

name: Shimek State Forest
notes: State forest is divided into 5 units. Camping is available. Several areas to activate in each unit.

name: Stephens State Forest
notes: Easy enough to find the official sign, but roads into the forest are narrow and unimproved, so best wait for dry weather. Some lumber cutting activity in certain areas of the park. Primitive campground has picnic tables.

name: White Pine Hollow State Forest
notes: Note this entity is White Pine Hollow State Forest which borders White Pine Hollow State Preserve. Access road (White Pine Lane) from the south.

name: Yellow River State Forest
notes: Yellow River State Forest is comprised of several distributed "units". Nice park with a variety of places to activate. It is adjacent to Effigy Mounds National Monument K-0922 to the south.

name: General C. C. Andrews State Forest
Lake of the Woods State Forest
Richard J. Dorer Memorial Hardwood State Forest
Busiek State Forest
notes: Much of this park is at lower elevations and the main parking lot is under the highway overpass. Some hiking trails to higher elevations on the western side. Large shooting range and equestrian activity.

name: Lester R. Davis Memorial State Forest
notes: Literally across the road from Prairie State Park, this is a small parking lot, a sign, and a big rock. Easy and obvious to find.

name: Reifsnider State Forest
notes: Dense forest and a large shooting range. Generally busy park, especially at peak times. Elevations vary widely, but tend to get lower as you go further into the park. Enough room near the entrance to activate/park.

name: Vanderhoef (Archie and Gracie) Memorial State Forest
notes: Small park with one parking lot and circle turnaround, and a few hiking trails. Easy to find, good signage.

name: Murphy (John F.) Memorial State Forest
notes: Primarily a wildlife area. Small parking lot on a county road, easy to spot. Can also hike inland to activate. don't be frightened...this park is on a regular low-altitude training route for A-10's from the nearby AF base.

name: Rand Bar Wildlife Management Area
notes: Bordered by private lands, the Missouri River, and the Desoto NWR, the only "normal access" would be to hike 0.75 mile from Desoto NWR. Note that off-road areas of Desoto NWR are seasonally closed, so check Desoto website for access dates. See DNR map.

name: Brule River State Forest
notes: Vehicle sticker required for campgrounds. Limited hours.

name: Coulee Experimental State Forest
notes: Limited hours.

name: Havenwoods State Forest
notes: Havenwoods State Forest is Wisconsin’s only urban state forest, featuring 237 acres of grasslands, woods and wetlands in the city of Milwaukee. Hours are 6am-8pm. No vehicle pass required. See website for additional details.

name: Governor Earl Peshtigo River State Forest
notes: Vehicle sticker is required for campground. Limited hours.

name: Niobrara National Wild and Scenic River
Sherman Reservoir State Recreation Area
notes: Park has several spacious parking lots on the south side at good elevation overlooking the lake.

name: White Nursery State Forest
notes: Developed, operating state tree nursery. A few parking lots along main road through the park.

name: Holland State Forest
notes: This park has only one parking spot, and it is at the bottom of a valley with over 100ft walls. Feels dark on a sunny day. You can also hike to the top of the hill to activate at higher elevation.

name: Funk Memorial State Forest
notes: This park has three separate tracts. Research carefully on Google Earth before activating to know where you will go.

name: Writing Rock State Historic Site
notes: Picnic tables in a grove of trees, picnic shelters, a building with a kitchen, fireplace, playground equipment, restrooms, and a parking lot. The two boulders are enclosed in a shelter and protected by iron bars.

name: Lower Wisconsin State Riverway State Park
notes: Limited hours.

name: Fisher Grove State Park
notes: Year-round. Between Oct. 1 and April 30, showers, flush toilets and other water systems may be closed

name: Spirit Mound Historic Prairie State Park
notes: No entrance fee required.

name: Olive Creek Lake State Recreation Area
Wagon Train Lake State Recreation Area
Lake Minatare State Recreation Area
notes: Closed to public access from October 15 to January 15. Does not share land with K-0445.

name: Standing Bear Lake State Recreation Area
Lake Zorinsky State Park
notes: Connected to Omaha walk/bike trail system. Day use only.

name: Alexandria Lakes State Recreation Area
notes: Nice park. Vehicle entry fee required.

name: Box Butte Reservoir State Recreation Area
Red Willow Reservoir State Recreation Area
Verdon Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Side road-side lake park with several good activating spots.

name: Little Turtle State Recreation Area
notes: Bordered by JE Roush Lake and Wabash River to the North, Division Rd to the South, Warren Rd to the West and N County Rd 200 to the East. Co-Located with J.E. Roush Lake FWA (K-4208)

name: Kil-So-Quah State Recreation Area
notes: Possibly Co-Located within J.E. Roush Lake SFWA (K-4208)

name: Lieber State Recreation Area
notes: Co-Located with Cagles Mill Lake SRA (K-4163)

name: Raccoon Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Co-Located with Cecil M Harden Lake SRA (K-4164)

name: Cartop State Recreation Area
notes: Small section unlabeled on map Northwest of Paynetown SRA.

name: Angeline State Conservation Area
notes: This is a smaller park with scenic lookouts, trails, and equestrian.

name: Atlanta Wildlife Area
notes: Numerous parking lots and roads around the lake.

name: Blind Pony State Conservation Area
notes: Scenic lake, easy to find...two main parking areas, with some shoreline open areas and picnic tables.

name: August A. Busch Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: No lack of activating spots. Numerous small lakes with parking lots. Hiking trails and archery range.

name: Grand Pass State Conservation Area
notes: Large wetlands park with numerous parking lots, BUT the levees and wetlands are constantly changing so only the eastern parking lots are stable from season to season.

name: Fountain Grove State Conservation Area
notes: Expansive area of lakes and wetlands. Several causeways across the park. Several parking lots.

name: Hartell (Ronald and Maude) State Conservation Area
notes: Depending on time of year or week, this is a quaint, smaller park with smaller lakes and several parking lots. Some picnic areas. Campground. Fishing is pretty good as well.

name: Hunnewell Lake State Conservation Area
notes: A very scenic, peaceful lake park with very nice shorelines and several parking lots around the perimeter of the park. A few grassy fishing jetties that can be activated.

name: Indian Trail State Conservation Area
notes: Forested, roads, occasional parking lots. Research on Google Earth before activating.

name: Lake Paho State Conservation Area
notes: A short and a long road on east and west shores respectively. The long road has the higher elevations and better parking lots. Good shoreline areas for activating and fishing.

name: Little Dixie Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Very nice lake park with two large parking areas. Nice open shoreline areas.

name: Lost Valley State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: This area has been subject to changes as to its status. The State website doesn't say anything, but tourist sites say it is closed. There are parking lots on the bluff and outside the main gate that are inside the park. Research the park.

name: Montrose State Conservation Area
notes: Modest park, with several parking lots and some primitive camping. Good activating site on the southern shoreline boat launch area.

name: Nodaway State Conservation Area
notes: Many perimeter parking lots and boat launches. There is a parking lot on the west border road that is an elevated overlook of the entire park. Good activating spot.

name: Platte Falls State Conservation Area
notes: Research and KNOW where you are going before activating. Many access points and parking lots around the large perimeter. Some may be very isolated. Also has archery and shotgun ranges, and the river is floatable.

name: Pony Express Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Nice smaller lake park. Easy access. Lots of maintained lakeshore to set up. A few parking lots. Fishing is easy access.

name: James A. Reed Memorial Wildlife Area
notes: Tends to be a training park for the state, so new agents may question occasionally. The key is having a small footprint! Lots of parking lots overlooking lakes!

name: Jay Nixon State Park
notes: This is one of four Missouri parks that have not been developed. Experience shows that rangers allow hiking in and out for day use. Currently, Jay Nixon can ONLY be reached via the Ozark Trail...approx 11 mile challenging roundtrip hike from Shut-Ins SP.

name: Shepherd of the Hills State Park
notes: This is one of four Missouri parks that have not been developed. Experience shows that rangers allow hiking in and out for day use or gate activations. Name changed May 2022 from Ozark Mountain.

name: Roger Pryor Pioneer Backcountry State Park
notes: This is primarily a backcountry hiking park.

name: Bruce R. Watkins Cultural Heritage Center State Park
notes: This is a city-center site and is essentially a concrete parking lot for the museum. Automobile activation or very limited footprint...no choice. Busy, high-visibility spot.

name: Little Jerusalem Badlands State Park
notes: Good sized parking lot for activation. May be activated on foot via marked trails only.

name: Flint Hills Trail State Park
notes: Research the park to find the best location for your activation before leaving. The Osawatomie trail head has limited parking, but can be acceptable during low activity times.

name: Badger Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Open park with several parking lots, fields, nice lake. Not much development.

name: Blood Run State Historic Site
notes: Historic site with no amenities along the Big Sioux River. Small gravel parking area maybe best. Take care if activating elsewhere.

name: Brushy Creek State Recreation Area
notes: Nice park, feels more like a State Park...lots of good activating options.

name: Emerson Bay State Recreation Area
notes: Small park with neat picnic areas and parking lots.

name: Fairport State Recreation Area
notes: Very small park with campground and boat launch along Mississippi.

name: Fort Atkinson State Preserve
notes: Small, historic abandon military fort with limited activation locations.

name: Lower Gar State Recreation Area
notes: Small drive-through park. Several parking lots and picnic areas.

name: Templar State Recreation Area
notes: Small State Rec Area. Lots of parking and nice grounds for activating options.

name: Volga River State Recreation Area
notes: Park has two campgrounds. Several trails meander through the park and parking scattered throughout park. There is a shelter near the boat ramp by Volga Lake.

name: Wilson Island State Recreation Area
notes: This park's access is at the intersection of the Southern entrance to the Desoto NWR. Basic park with usual amenities.

name: Bixby State Preserve
notes: Single parking lot, with an old shelter next to a stream.

name: Little River Wildlife Management Area
notes: Research carefully before activating. Lots of private land in between public accesses.

name: Turtle Mountain State Forest
notes: Turtle Mountain State Forest, encompasses over 7,500 acres of pristine forests, wetlands, and grasslands. https://www.ndsu.edu/sites/default/files/documents/Turtle_Mountain_Trail_Map.pdf

name: Homen State Forest
notes: Activator reports that there are no signs showing "Homen State Forest". Pelican/Sandy Lake Rec Area is part of the forest and would be a good place to activate.

name: Mouse River State Forest
notes: Unknow if any signage exists. The GPS position is correct. Unknown if any entry point exist.

name: Tetrault Woods State Forest
notes: Check out scenic overlook on northwest side of forest. No facilities.

name: Nowesta Memorial Grove State Forest
notes: 12 acres. Small roadside park.

name: Sheyenne River State Forest
notes: The state forest is bisected by 4 miles of the North Country National Scenic Trail, US-4239

name: Crow Flies High State Recreation Area

name: Guy B Park State Conservation Area

name: Kendzora State Conservation Area

name: Cooley Lake State Conservation Area

name: Amarugia Highlands State Conservation Area
notes: The county roads to and from can be challenging by season, but the park is well-maintained. Several very open parking lots with boat ramps and fishing access.

name: Maple Leaf Lake State Conservation Area

name: Crooked River State Conservation Area

name: Poague Haysler State Conservation Area
notes: Several lake causeways and several primitive parking areas. Need to pick your activating sots. Good fishing.

name: Harmony Mission Lake State Conservation Area
notes: The county roads get worse and worse, until you break out to a beautiful park, lake and large paved parking lot with fishing and boat access.

name: Schell-Osage State Conservation Area

name: King Lake State Conservation Area

name: Lamine River State Conservation Area

name: Ben Branch Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Two parking lots to activate from...one on the west bluff and another near the boat ramp. Very scenic lake.

name: Apple Creek State Conservation Area

name: Duck Creek State Conservation Area

name: Daniel Boone State Conservation Area

name: General Watkins State Conservation Area

name: Little Black State Conservation Area

name: Otter Slough State Conservation Area

name: Coon Island State Conservation Area

name: Huzzah State Conservation Area

name: Meramec State Conservation Area

name: Magnolia Hollow State Conservation Area

name: Whetstone Creek State Conservation Area

name: Bridger State Conservation Area

name: Dupont Reservation Conservation Reserve

name: Little Lost Creek Conservation Reserve

name: American Horse State Fishing Lake

name: Lake Elmer State Fishing Lake

name: Brickyard Hill State Conservation Area
notes: The main entrance is on Charity Lake with parking area, open area and fishing access. The road that goes northwest of the lake stops at a higher elevation parking lot.

name: Corning State Conservation Area
notes: Suggest you research your route on Google Earth. Google Maps will get you lost on this one. Easiest to access from the nearby town of Corning.

name: Deroin Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Be advised that access is difficult due to construction. You may be able to get inside the boundary via some local roads. You may need an accurate map, SUV, and patience to get inside the boundary on this one. Or go by boat on the river.

name: Lower Hamburg Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Flood reconstruction continues, and only one open access road was found...it's the one that's on the state line into the northeast corner of the park and crosses over the levee. All other access roads are closed for construction or private property.

name: Rush Bottoms State Conservation Area
notes: Research your route on Google Earth for this one. Check website for flooding and other closures. Best access is the eastern river shore east of Rulo...underpass to the park levee to activate.

name: Star School Hill Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: This park has two tracts about two miles apart...each with a very small up-sloped parking lot. Not ideal activating except for a short time.

name: Wolf Creek Bend State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find at the end of long gravel roads...but research your route on Google Earth for this one.

name: B.K. Leach Memorial State Conservation Area
notes: This is mostly a wetlands park...subject to seasonal flooding. Research or call ahead before a long drive.

name: Bee Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Don't blink or you'll miss it. Only one parking lot, not far off the main highway.

name: Bethel Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Relatively close to the highway, and a single parking lot on the southern border county road. Easy to find. Roads can be rough in the springtime.

name: Black Island State Conservation Area
notes: There are roads, but access to this area is not obvious. Plan you route on Google Earth before activating, and expect certain wetland features may change seasonally.

name: Bonanza State Conservation Area
notes: Park has two tracts, with the eastern tract being the most developed one. Surprisingly scenic in spite of the map. Several parking lots.

name: Bristow State Conservation Area
notes: One of the basic "square" prairie conservation areas...only one parking lot on the eat border. Easy to find.

name: Buffalo Wallow State Conservation Area
notes: This park has three discontinous tracts, but it can be tricky to find it. Not many signs. Need to research the park on Google Earth before you activate.

name: Bunch Hollow State Conservation Area
notes: Best to stay on the eastern roads/approaches. The west side can become impassable during wet seasons. Most of the parking lots and fishing spots are on the east side.

name: Caney State Conservation Area
notes: Larger hilly area with several roads and some parking lots, as well as hiking trails and camping. The east entrance is apparently not public, but there is a shooting range on the west entrance that is a good activating spot.

name: Clear Creek State Conservation Area
notes: This park is not well marked, irregularly shaped, so tricky to find it and it is surrounded by private lands. Research it on Google Earth!

name: Cuivre Island State Conservation Area
notes: Mainland tract is small with the only parking lot. The rest or the park consists of two forested islands.

name: Dorris Creek Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot on the south western corner. Easy to find. Out of the way park. Open prairie.

name: Fourche Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Five separate tracts with no parking lots...be prepared for alternative activating techniques. Research your activating spot before you get there.

name: Girvin State Conservation Area
notes: The MDC asks that you stay off the access road when it is wet...which means seasonal access may be restricted...and only known when you get there. Plan activations during dry weather.

name: Honey Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Larger conservation area with equestrian themes and facilities. Large parking lots on higher elevations.

name: Ketcherside Mountain State Conservation Area
notes: This area has several separate tracts...some accessible on the Ozark Trail...some accessible by road. Very irregular outline bordered by private lands. Research carefully before activating.

name: Little Compton Lake State Conservation Area
notes: Smaller park but very nice, clean and nice fishing lake with jetties. Two main parking lots on opposite shores.

name: Mincy State Conservation Area
notes: This is administratively ONE Conservation area that is split into two flanks. Lots of parking lots. Generally lower elevation and subject to flooding. Check before travel.

name: Mo-No-I Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find square conservation area. Road can be difficult in the spring. One parking lot on the southern border.

name: Monkey Mountain State Conservation Area
notes: Suggest activating of the parking lots on the north end of the park. Parking lots and roads on the south border are at lower elevations and in poor condition.

name: Osage Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: Easy to find park, a few parking lots.

name: Pa Sole Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: A single parking lot area...open prairie. Easy to find. RF quiet spot.

name: Pelican Island State Conservation Area

name: Ranacker State Conservation Area

name: Redwing Prairie State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot on the southern border, but parking lot is tiny...first come, first served...

name: Riverbreaks State Conservation Area
notes: Several parking lots, open areas, primitive camping, and a large DIY shooting range.

name: Treaty Line State Conservation Area
notes: Large parking lot on the north-west corner...easy to find.

name: White Ranch State Conservation Area
notes: The lake parking lot at the center of the park is the best activating spot.

name: Worthwine Island State Conservation Area
notes: Two easy to find parking lots. Close to river so check website for flooding and other closures.

name: Yellow Creek State Conservation Area

name: World Shooting Complex State Recreation Area

name: Stoney Point Prairie State Conservation Area

name: Sky Prairie State Conservation Area

notes: Limited hours. The parking lots are NOT VALID activation locations. They are not inside of the boundary of the state natural area. Walk in activation only. Check website for for more information and a detailed map.

name: Mussel Fork State Conservation Area
notes: Large Conservation Area, next to Hwy 36. Parking lot about 100 yds from Hwy 36 on Noble Drive. Not scenic, but it works. Deeper in the park, there are small fishing ponds and other recreational facilities.

name: Union Ridge State Conservation Area
notes: Larger Conservation Area with multiple access points and parking lots. If you don't like one, just drive another mile to the next one. Some parking lots at higher elevations, some in valleys.

name: Sugar Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Typical conservation area with forests and prairie, several parking lots and a DIY shooting range.

name: Indian Hills State Conservation Area
notes: Several parking lots and some primitive camping areas.

name: Hidden Hollow State Conservation Area
notes: Wooded park with three parking lots, and a few roads.

name: LaBarque Creek State Conservation Area
notes: One parking lot and some hiking trails.

name: Big Creek State Conservation Area
notes: Some perimeter parking lots, hiking trails.

name: Shoemaker State Conservation Area
notes: Small generic Conservation Area...two small parking lots. Easy to miss.

name: Ruth and Paul Henning Conservation Area State Conservation Area
notes: This Conservation Area surrounds (but, oddly, does not include) the White River Balds Natural Area. Several good parking lots and access points. Easy to find.

name: White River Balds Natural Area State Conservation Area
notes: This Natural Area is included but not part of K-8510. It is managed by K-8510. Generally higher elevation. Proximity to tourist areas, so can be busy.

name: Springfield Conservation Nature Center State Conservation Area
notes: In-town park with large parking lot and several manicured walking trails...some open area. Can be very busy during peak times.

name: Stewart Lake National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

name: White Lake National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWRs, practicing a small, non-invasive activating footprint that does not have ANY impact on grounds, trees, wildlife, other visitors, etc., is important to both the NWR and POTA missions. Check-in with NWR Ranger station strongly advised.

name: Bismarck-Deadwood Stage Trail State Historic Site
notes: A marker at a roadside stop on the north side of Highway 21.

name: Camp Atchison State Historic Site
notes: A fieldstone monument and an aluminum marker.

name: Camp Buell State Historic Site
notes: A marker and a sign.

name: Camp Hancock State Historic Site
notes: Picnic area. No vehicle parking available within park boundary, equipment must be carried in.

name: Cannonball Stage Station State Historic Site
notes: A quiet park on the east bank of the Cannonball River with a hand-pump water fountain and picnic table.

name: Chateau De Mores State Historic Site
notes: Consists of the museum house (admission fee), a downtown Medora Memorial Park, and the Chimney Park on the west edge of Medora.

name: David Thompson State Historic Site
notes: A granite globe atop a rectangular granite base, the site is enclosed by a barbed wire fence.

name: Double Ditch Indian Village State Historic Site
notes: Interpretive Signage, Walking Paths, No Facilities

name: Fort Buford State Historic Site
notes: Modern facilities on site, picnic area and campgrounds

name: Fort Clark State Historic Site
notes: Modern restrooms, a picnic area, and an observation deck are located at the site.

name: Fort Dilts State Historic Site
notes: A flagpole, a site marker, a registration box, a barbed wire fence, and an interpretive sign north of the fortification remains.

name: Fort Mandan Overlook State Historic Site
notes: There are two markers at the site, one identifying it as a state historic site and the other placed there by the Order of the Masons.

name: Fort Rice State Historic Site
notes: Parking space is available, but there are no visitor services. There is a marker on the site. The campground is not part of the site. It is county owned.

name: Fort Totten State Historic Site
notes: Grounds are open year-round, Monday - Friday, 9 a.m.-5 p.m.

name: Gingras Trading Post State Historic Site
notes: Site grounds with outdoor interpretive signs open year-round.

name: Hudson Townsite State Historic Site
notes: There is a fenced in Marker. The road in front of the site is also part of the site. Acivate this site on the road.

name: Huff Indian Village State Historic Site
notes: Open year round.

name: Killdeer Mountain Battlefield State Historic Site
notes: A sandstone slab monument and flagpole mark the battlefield and an unpaved parking lot is separated from the site by a log barrier.

name: Lake Jessie State Historic Site
notes: An aluminum cast marker on a fieldstone, a concrete monument, and a flagpole.

name: Lake Johnson State Historic Site
notes: Located 7 miles southwest of Cooperstown, ND. A headstone and flagpole.

name: Maple Creek Crossing State Historic Site
notes: Located 3 miles south of Chaffee, ND. Although no visitor services are available and the ford is not visible from the site, the state property is attractive, well tended, and accessible year-round. There is a marker on a masonry base.

name: Menoken Indian Village State Historic Site
notes: Located 1 1/2 miles northeast of Menoken, 10 miles east of Bismarck, ND. Open year round.

name: Missouri-Yellowstone Confluence Interpretive Center State Historic Site
notes: Oct. 1–April 30 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Tues.–Sat. May 1–Sept. 30 9 a.m.–5 p.m. Daily We are closed the following holidays: New Year's Eve & Day Martin Luther King Jr. Day Presidents Day Good Friday Veterans Day Thanksgiving Day & Black Friday Christmas Eve & Day

name: November 33 Launch Facility State Historic Site
notes: The Ronald Reagan Minuteman Missile State Historic Site, November-33, Check website for opening and closing times and fees.

name: Oak Lawn Church State Historic Site
notes: Located about 11 miles south of Walhalla, ND. A peaceful cemetery and a fieldstone marker. Please be respectful.

name: Pembina State Museum State Historic Site
notes: Situated just off Interstate 29, Exit 215, in Pembina, ND. See hours on web page.

name: Oscar-Zero Missile Alert Facility State Historic Site
notes: Oscar-Zero is located four miles north of Cooperstown on Highway 45

name: Steamboat Warehouse State Historic Site
notes: Located located on the east bank of the Missouri River in Bismarck across the road from the water treatment plant on River Road (Highway 1804). A fieldstone monument with an aluminum plaque and a small parking area on the west side of the road.

name: Wadeson Cabin State Historic Site
notes: Located on the east bank of the Sheyenne River near Kathryn, ND. A marker and a small parking area on the north side of the building.

name: Welk Homestead State Historic Site
notes: From Strasburg: North 1/2 mile on US 83 to 88th Street. Approximately 2 miles to 8th Avenue SE. Farm driveway is on the east side of the road. Closed Until Spring. Memorial Day Weekend - Labor Day: Thursday-Sunday, 10 a.m.-5 p.m.

name: Whitestone Hill State Historic Site
notes: Located 23 miles southeast of Kulm, ND. Open year round.

name: Missouri River State Natural Area
notes: No facilities

notes: Fees, None. There is no potable water or restrooms available. Open year-round. Road become impassable during inclement weather and after heavy rains.

notes: During the rainy season, normally in spring and late summer, the roads can get slippery and rutted. During winter, the area can be unreachable. Check with the BLM about road conditions before your visit

notes: Camping available.

name: Lake Watonga State Fishing Lake

notes: No facilities.

notes: No facilities. From HWY 62 take N4616 RD south which leads to the WMA parking lot.
