notes: No facilities.

name: Haskell Noyes Memorial Woods State Natural Area
notes: Smaller State Natural Area. Wisconsin vehicle admission pass or National Park pass required. Parking area located along County Road GGG. This park is fully inside of the Kettle Moraine State Forest US-4352.

name: Waterloo Prairie State Natural Area
notes: 4 distinct areas of land in Waterloo Prairie State Natural Area. Given coordinates is one of them. Check the website for more information and maps.

name: Scuppernong Prairie State Natural Area
notes: Roadside parking only. Parking area to the south on N isn't in the boundaries of the park. Scuppernong Prairie supports a diversity of wet-mesic prairie species on level, poorly-drained ground in the Scuppernong Basin. See website for additional details.

name: Vernon State Wildlife Area
notes: Vernon Wildlife Area is a 4,655-acre property (4,154 acres owned and 501 acres leased) located just north of Mukwonago in eastern Waukesha County. See website for additional details.

name: Tichigan State Wildlife Area
notes: Tichigan Wildlife Area is a 1,280-acre property in northwest Racine County. See website for additional details.

name: Great River State Trail
notes: Limited hours. A state trail pass is required for bicycling. Check website for details.

name: La Crosse River State Trail
notes: Limited hours. A state trail pass is required for bicycling. Check website for details.

name: Butterfield State Trail
notes: This is a trail so there are many ways and places to activate. Here is another web page with routes.https://arkansasheritagetrails.com/Butterfield/

name: Lower White Oak Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Several places around the lake to activate from your car or boat. There is an island you could get out and set up on but probably not very easy.

name: Saracen State Trail
notes: Nice activation spot from your car in the paring lot. The pavilion may be reserved but can be used otherwise.

name: Lake Conway State Recreation Area
notes: Lake Conway may be activated by boat or from one of the parking areas adjacent to the boat ramp.

name: Cox Creek Lake State Recreation Area
notes: You will find boating, Camping, kayaking and fishing here. It seems to be a good activation site.

name: Lake Elmdale State Recreation Area
notes: Access to the lake is by a concrete ramp with parking area near the dam on the lake’s northwest side. There is another access point in the midsection of the lake. Both are reached off Elm Springs Road between Elm Springs and Springdale. The road intersect

name: Lake Hinkle State Recreation Area
notes: From Waldron, Arkansas, drive west on Highway 248 for 11-1/2 miles. Turn east (left) on County Road 10 for the entrance of the boating, swimming and camping areas.

name: Lake Jack Nolen State Recreation Area
Huckabee Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Large parking area with cell service. Limited shade during the middle of the day.

name: Constitution Hall State Historic Site
notes: This is a small in-town park. There is an accessible parking lot in the back yard from the laneway that has been used for activating on Mondays and Tuesdays and hours when the museum is closed. Otherwise ask for permission to set up.

name: Fort Hays State Historic Site
notes: Open 10 a.m. - 5 p.m. Wednesday - Saturday. See website for further information.

name: Grinter Place State Historic Site
notes: Very large parking lot up high and in the clear. Easy to find next to the main road and not far from HWY 435.

name: Hollenberg Pony Express Station State Historic Site
notes: Nice park out in middle of prairie expanse. Very nice open area and elevated (as far as can be in KS) parking lot to activate from.

name: Kaw Mission State Historic Site
notes: Building is temporarily closed. Parking is available in front of the Mission.

name: Pawnee Indian Museum State Historic Site
notes: Grounds are open even though the museum building may not be. Extensive walking paths and manicured grounds...large paved parking lot.

name: Red Rocks State Historic Site
notes: This is an in-town park...very tiny garage entrance parking for one vehicle. However, the road in front of the building has a sign that restricts parking to Historic Site visitors only, and the historical marker is on the curb.

name: Cottonwood Ranch State Historic Site
notes: The exterior of the property is open dawn until dusk, daily. The ranch house itself is available for guided tours only.

name: First Territorial Capitol State Historic Site
notes: This park in on a military station. Access is restricted/controlled, but possible as long as the published procedure is followed. Military ID preferred, but civilians with specified documents can access. Read information carefully before attempting.

name: Goodnow House State Historic Site
notes: Open daily 9:00 - 5:00 Tuesday through Friday. Open 2:00 - 5:00 Saturday & Sunday. Closed holidays.

name: John Brown Museum State Historic Site
notes: This park is in town, but the grounds are large and the various parking lots are good size. The west side closest to the museum is higher elevation. Noise levels not too bad for in-town.

name: Shawnee Indian Mission State Historic Site
notes: Small limited parking lot in a residential area. Mobile activation favored. Very limited open space around the yard for other options.

name: Iowa and Sac & Fox Mission State Historic Site
notes: Small property at the end of a laneway. Parking lot and one picnic table. Can be semi-abandoned certain times of the year, but otherwise easy to find and access.

name: Marais des Cygnes Massacre State Historic Site
notes: Out-of-the-way park on gravel roads, but the park area itself is on an elevated bluff, obvious sign, with picnic tables and open areas to activate. Some park roadways may be washed out by rain, so be cautious.

name: Pawnee Rock State Historic Site
notes: Parking available.

name: Hendrickson Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Wildlife management area surrounding Hendrickson Marsh Lake. Several gravel parking areas and a boat launch.

name: Colfax Wildlife Management Area
notes: The park is best found on maps...the DNR website is not very detailed on this one. A variety of hunting websites show it well. It is very poorly identified, so be sure where you are.

name: Redbird Farms Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA is on both sides of the road and each side has parking for activations.

name: Hawkeye Wildlife Management Area
notes: NOTE: Most of the land here is US Army Corps of Engineers which is OUTSIDE of the POTA entity. A small section is state owned and valid for POTA. See the map to the assessor's page. Do not operate on USACE land. The pin on the POTA map is accurate.

name: Hanging Rock Ridge Wildlife Management Area
notes: Relatively small WMA with a single parking lot.

name: Salt Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small, wooded WMA hunting area with a single parking entrance on the south side.

name: Hawthorne Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small WMA lake with several parking areas for activations.

name: Fox River Wildlife Management Area
notes: As with all Refuges, no impact setup and small footprints are best. Reasonably well identified and good parking lots.

name: Lake Sugema Wildlife Management Area
notes: K-4573 intersects some areas of this WMA for a possible 2-fer. Check the K-4573 map for details.

name: Sand Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Easy to miss. Roads can be rough by season.

name: Fogle Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Rural WMA with a parking area for activation. Note that the WMA is adjacent to a county park with the Fogle Lake name. Check the DNR map for the location of the WMA.

name: Kellerton Bird Wildlife Management Area
notes: Bird conservation area near Kellerton. Private property around, so please research before activating.

name: Lake Shawtee Wildlife Management Area
notes: Wildlife area - public hunting grounds. Relatively elevated parking areas from surrounding terrain are great for activations.

name: Cooper Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Easy to find with Google Maps/GPS, but very little signage. One parking area on the east border with DNR signs. Easy to activate, out of the way, quiet.

name: Forney's Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Large WMA, but no visible lake other than an expansive marsh. Some parking lots on the south and east borders, but the main circle parking is on the south border.

name: Green Hollow Wildlife Management Area
notes: Although the map does not show it, there is a parking lot about half-way up the east border road. This parking lot has the WMA sign and is at a high elevation spot for the area/park. Ideal activation spot.

name: St Mary's Island Wildlife Management Area
notes: Research/plan carefully on Google Earth and DNR maps before activating...some accesses are better than others.

name: Nobles Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small parking lot next to an oxbow lake. Simple small park...no frills, but peaceful and easy to find.

name: Keg Creek lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Nice, straightforward, smaller park in view of the highway. Small parking lot overlooking a small pond. Easy to find.

name: Rosenow Timber Wildlife Management Area
notes: Forest WMA with limited parking spots.

name: Round Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: A small parking lot off the rural road...well-marked, but easy to miss if you are not looking for it.

name: Beaver Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Typical WMA with nice lake and parking lots. The DNR site mentions picnic areas but there are no picnic tables. There is a campground adjacent to but not within the park.

name: Three Mile Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking for the WMA on the West and South sides of the lake. The County Parks on the North and East sides of the lake are not within the WMA. A 2-fer is possible with K-4573 only at the area east of the intersection of 12 Mile Lake Ave and 148th St.

name: Elk Grove Wildlife Management Area
notes: Forested WMA - hunting area with several gravel parking area for activations.

name: Harrier Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Not hard to find. As this is part of the US FWS system, it also counts for US-0270. Check the maps for both.

name: Finn Pond Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small WMA parking lot next to highway.

name: Goose Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small lake surrounded by wildlife management area. Parking areas and boat launches available for activations.

name: Tomahawk Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: Several small parking lots, easy to miss. Google may take you to a parking lot that is actually private property. Be sure to activate from the public hunting lot.

name: Big Sioux River Wildlife Management Area
notes: This WMA has a chain of 4 units along the Big Sioux River. Typical WMA parking is available for activations.

name: Morse Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small lake with access road along east side of lake. Parking / boat launch on south side works for POTA.

name: Lower Morse Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Typical Iowa DNR wildlife management area. Note that the parking lot is marked on the map for this location. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for US-0270.

name: Elm Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: There are two public access boat launch areas for this lake. The launch at the north end isolated... a good spot for POTA. The launch on the east side of the lake is surrounded by houses. DNR officer also recommended the north spot was best for POTA.

name: Buffalo Basins Wildlife Management Area
notes: DNR wildlife area. Grass parking entrance is on highway (Balsam Ave) along the west edge of the WMA.

name: Waterman Prarie Complex Wildlife Management Area
notes: Well-marked parking lot on the road to Peterson, but not obvious to find. It is in a valley.

name: Wittrock Indian Village State Preserve
notes: Not well-marked archeology site. Must hike (~.5 mi) to reach the State Preserve from the East. There is a small indent off the road at the bottom of the hill. Suggest parking on the road and hiking in to be in boundary. Private land East and North.

name: Little Storm Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: The parking lot and sign are on the inside of a busy local street, across from the beach park. Suggest turning into the beach park and then crossing to the WMA parking when traffic allows. Otherwise, small dirt parking lot, no frills.

name: Rush Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Well-marked on roadside, but only a rough parking lot at the end of a two-rut dirt road...lots of wildlife. This site is in Osceola county near Ocheyedan. Another area named Rush Lake is in Palo Alto county.

name: Deweys Pasture Wildlife Management Area
notes: Need to research the boundaries carefully, but Dewey and Barringers are across the road from each other.

name: Eagle Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: Fishing area in Hancock county. At least two parking areas for activations. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for K-0270.

name: Blue Wing Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with private property nearby. Please research before activating. There are more than two locations in Iowa called "Blue Wing Marsh", but only this one is managed by Iowa DNR.

name: Barringers Slough Wildlife Management Area
notes: Need to research maps carefully, but Dewey and Barringers are across the road from each other at one spot.

name: Teal Basins State Waterfowl Management Area
notes: Pheasant hunting grounds with a single gravel parking area on the South side of the Waterfowl Production Area. As this is part of the US FWS Iowa Wetland Management District, it also counts for K-0270.

name: Wapsi Flats Wildlife Management Area
notes: Rural WMA hunting grounds with 2 sections. Small gravel parking lots.

name: Sweet Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with several parking locations for activations including a boat ramp on the south end.

name: Turkey River Wildlife Management Area
notes: Southern parking area on King's Road in the middle of this WMA is easily accessed. If not available, there are two additional parking areas at the north end of the WMA.

name: Cardinal Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along the Turkey River with several parking areas.

name: Bluffton Fir Stand State Preserve
notes: Public hunting grounds surrounding the town of Bluffton. Several parking lots / boat launches are within the preserve.

name: Pine Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking lot down in the valley on the east end of the WMA or off the road that borders the south

name: Coon Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 3 parking areas for this WMA. The lot on the SouthWest side of the WMA is not near the creek itself but is substantially more elevated than the other 2.

name: South Pine Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Gravel parking lot access to WMA.

name: Canoe Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Parking at the confluence of Canoe Creek and Upper Iowa River. Busy area during fishing season.

name: North Bear Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 5 parking lots along the creek for this WMA. This entity is adjacent to South Bear Creek WMA. They do not overlap.

name: South Bear Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: 7 parking lots along the South Bear Creek WMA.

name: Big Mill Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Trout stream WMA. Parking areas for activation at both the north and south end of the WMA.

name: Barber Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Public hunting area north of the Wapsipinicon River. A few parking areas along a gravel road.

name: Lost Grove Lake Wildlife Management Area
notes: DNR lake with surrounding WMA (restored prairie). Several boat launches and parking areas available.

name: Wiese Slough Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along Cedar River with 4 parking areas and two boat ramps that may provide activation areas.

name: Red Cedar Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA along Cedar River near Cedar Bottoms WMA (K-9352). At least 2 parking areas on north side may be locations for activations.

name: Cedar Bottoms Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA is divided into 2 sections (on either side of Cedar River). Parking areas available on both may provide activation areas.

name: Cone Marsh Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with small parking lots and 2 boat ramps for activation areas.

name: Fox Hills Wildlife Management Area
notes: WMA with 2 sections along the river. At least 3 parking areas listed for potential activation spots. Forested, with private land nearby. Some parking areas are very small. Check the DNR maps not just Google maps for this one.

name: Danish Alps State Recreation Area
notes: Very nice lakeshore rec area...several potential activating spots. A park entry permit is required, so combining activating other nearby parks like Ponca SP is suggested.

name: Lewis and Clark Lake State Recreation Area
Riverview State Recreation Area
notes: Do not follow Google Maps/GPS that follows a private industrial road along the river...instead start from downtown Neb City and go east from there through residential areas. Park permit is required and must be purchased off-site ahead of arrival.

name: Rock Creek Station State Recreation Area
notes: Park does NOT share land with K-2623. K-4578 does not go through this entity. No dual/triple activation possible. Vehicle entry fee required.

name: Rockford Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Park access fee required for this park. Purchase on-line or locally ahead of time.

name: Leadville National Fish Hatchery National Wildlife Management Area
notes: Leadville National Fish Hatchery, established in 1889, is the second oldest federally operated fish hatchery in operation today.

name: Indian Peaks Wilderness National Conservation Area
Gunnison Gorge BLM National Conservation Area
McInnis Canyons BLM National Conservation Area
North Sand Hills BLM National Recreation Area
Hardscrabble-East Eagle BLM National Recreation Area
notes: Camping is allowed outside of the Spring Creek area and in previously disturbed sites.

name: Wolford Mountain and Dam Site BLM National Recreation Area
notes: Wolford Mountain and Reservoir is stop 8 on the Rabbit Ears Birding Trail https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/rabbit-ears

name: Zapata Falls BLM National Recreation Area
Adams State Wildlife Area
notes: Must possess a valid hunting or fishing license or an SWA pass. Parking and restrooms available.

name: Adobe Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Must possess a valid hunting or fishing license or SWA pass. This is stop #3 on the Plover Colorado Birding Trail https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/site/adobe-creek-reservoir-blue-lake.

name: Alberta Park Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: Watch the boundary. The reservoir is the park. Legit. activations must be from within the boundaries, not the parking area. A valid hunting or fishing license or SWA pass is required for all visitors over 16 years of age.

name: Alma State Wildlife Area
notes: Must possess a hunting or fishing license or SWA pass.

name: Apishapa State Wildlife Area
notes: Apishapa SWA is also Stop #18 on the Spanish Peaks Birding Trail https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/spanish-peaks. Valid hunting, fishing license or SWA permit required for all persons over 16.

name: Basalt State Wildlife Area
notes: Activities: Hunting, Fishing, Picnicking, Nature Viewing, Shooting Range. Closed Dec. 1–July 15. A valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required for everyone 16 or older accessing this state wildlife area.

name: Beaver Creek Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: The park is a reservoir.The lake is the park.Parking, camping, picnic sites are not in this park.Valid hunting/fishing license or SWA pass required for all persons 16 or older. Stop 8 on the Wolf Creek Trail https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/

name: Beaver Lake State Wildlife Area
notes: A valid hunting or fishing license or State Wildlife Area pass is required for all persons aged 16 or over.

name: Big Meadows Reservoir State Wildlife Area
Big Thompson Ponds State Wildlife Area
notes: Requires CO State Wildlife Pass or hunting/fishing license. Small parking lot accessible very close to I-25. On the east-side frontage road, find a small, unmarked, one-lane tunnel to cross under to the west side of I-25, then go north.

name: Boedecker Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: Requires CO State Wildlife Area Pass or hunting/fishing license. Large parking lot used for boat trailer parking. Very scenic.

name: Bosque Del Oso State Wildlife Area
notes: Access prohibited Dec. 1 through Mar. 31, except big game hunters. Valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass required. Stop 11 on the Spanish Peaks Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/spanish-peaks

name: Bravo State Wildlife Area
notes: A valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass is required for all persons 16 or over. Gathering any plant material is prohibited on this site.

name: Brown Lakes State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 10 on the Silver Thread Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/silver-thread. A valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass is required for all persons over 16 years old.

name: Clear Creek Reservoir State Wildlife Area
Coalbed Canyon State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 14 on the Canyons of the Ancients Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/western-colorado/canyon-of-the-ancients. All persons 16 or over must possess a valid fishing or hunting license or a SWA pass.

name: Coke Oven State Wildlife Area
notes: There is no signage at the property, so you will need to make sure you are completely within the State Wildlife Area. A valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass is required for all persons aged 16 and over.

name: Cottonwood State Wildlife Area
notes: Public access is prohibited from 9:00 pm to 3:00 am daily except when authorized by a night hunting permit. A valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass is required for all persons 16 or over.

name: Cowdrey Lake State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 7 on the North Park Birding Trail. https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/north-park. A valid hunting or fishing license or SWA passis required for all persons 16 or over .

name: Dan Noble State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 15 on the Lizard Head Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/lizard-head. A valid fishing or hunting license or State Wildlife Area pass is required for all persons age 16 or over.

name: Delaney Butte Lakes State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 14 on the North Park Colorado Birding Trail. https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/north-park/ A valid fishing or hunting license is required for all persons over 16 years of age.

name: Devil Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Access is via a steep, narrow road. There is limited space at the parking area. A valid hunting or fishing license or SWA pass is required for all persons age 16 or over.

name: Deweese Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 11 on the Greenhorn Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/rocky-mountains/greenhorn. All persons 16 or older must possess a valid fishing or hunting license or an SWA pass.

name: Dry Creek Basin State Wildlife Area
notes: This area is stop 11 on the Uncompahgre Birding Trail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/western-colorado/uncompahgre. A valid hunting or fishing license is required for all persons aged 16 and over.

name: Duck Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: A valid hunting or fishing license or State Wildlife Area pass is required for all persons 16 yeras of age or older.

name: Echo Canyon Reservoir State Wildlife Area
Four Mile State Wildlife Area
notes: Public access is by foot or horseback only. All persons 16 or older must possess a valid fishing or hunting license or a SWA pass.

name: Gypsum Ponds State Wildlife Area
notes: Activities: Hunting, Fishing & Nature Viewing. A valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required.

name: Horse Creek Reservoir State Wildlife Area
Hot Sulfur Springs State Wildlife Area
notes: Always be mindful of the wildlife - Do Not Disturb.

name: Joe Moore Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: A valid fishing or hunting license or a state wildlife area pass is required for all persons aged 16 and over.

name: Prewitt Reservoir State Wildlife Area
notes: This is stop 8 on the Playa BirdingTrail, https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/eastern-plains/playa. This park has several site-specific restrictions in addition to the requirement for a fishing or hunting license or SWA pass for persons over 16.

name: Timpas Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Timpas Creek SWA is walk-in. No vehicle access or parking in park. Valid hunting or fishing license or SWA pass required for access. Timpas Creek is stop 12 on the Pronghorn Birding Trail. https://coloradobirdingtrail.com/trail/eastern-plains/pronghorn

name: Wahatoya State Wildlife Area
notes: A valid fishing or hunting license or SWA pass is required for all persons 16 years of age or older accessing this property.

name: Williams Creek Reservoir State Wildlife Area
Windy Gap Watchable State Wildlife Area
Pecos Canyon State Park
notes: Just a short drive from Santa Fe and north of the Village of Pecos, this newly created (2019) state park will offer fishing, camping, hiking, and more!

name: Blue Mountain Natural Area
notes: trails for hikers and mountain bikers and a parking area will make this a good area to activate. Map of the area https://www.arkansasheritage.com/docs/default-source/anhc-maps/boundary-maps/blue-mountain-natural-area-3-18-22.pdf?sfvrsn=331650f_2&fbcl

name: Camden Expedition Scenic Highway State Trail
notes: This is a state trail with many historic markers and activation sites along its route. It intersects several other POTA parks and trails. Please check the web site for a great map.

name: Amache National Historic Site
notes: This is a newly created park (March 2022, Amache NHS Act). The site will convert from City/private ownership to NPS in 2022 and 2023. Several good parking spots, open areas. Limited facilites. Park website cautions about rough trails and rattlesnakes.

name: Lizard Mound State Park
notes: A Wisconsin DNR vehicle admission pass is required. Limited hours. Show respect for the area as it is a Native American burial ground. Check website for details

name: Savage Gulf State Park
notes: This is a very new (Sept '22) announce State Park in TN. Used to be a Natural Area. Official website should updated soon, but the existing NA website shows site info.

name: Lehigh Portland State Park
notes: Very new park in Kansas. Used to be a local trails park by the same name. Website and maps show it officially, but likely more well-defined maps to become available soon.

name: Katy Trail Rock Island Spur State Park
notes: Very new State Park. Used to be the Rock Island Spur of the Katy Trail State Park. This is a new, separate trail park, so not a 2-fer with Katy Trail...and the pin is placed at trail head in Windsor.

name: Decker Wildlife Management Area
notes: Newly created park. Reportedly has one parking lot, but observe/respect posted property and private property signage in vicinity.

name: Butterfield Overland National Historic Trail
notes: This is a very new NHT created in 2023. Please be aware that it will be some time before official trail markers appear, and as with all NHTs, activation must be on public property, even though much of the trail is on private lands. Research carefully!

name: 400 State Trail
notes: The entire length of the 22-mile trail follows along the river valley from Elroy to Reedsburg. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and horseback riding. See website for additional details.

name: Badger State Trail
notes: The Badger State Trail travels 40 miles between Madison and the Wisconsin-Illinois border. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and in-line skating. See website for additional details.

name: Bearskin State Trail
notes: Named for the Bearskin Creek the trail follows, this former railroad corridor is an opportunity to experience the Northwoods of Wisconsin. A state trail pass is required is required for bicycling. See website for additional details.

name: Buffalo River State Trail
notes: This trail in west-central Wisconsin follows the scenic Buffalo River valley for 36 miles between Mondovi and Fairchild. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and horseback riding. See website for additional details.

name: Capital City State Trail
notes: The Capital City State Trail is the link around and through Madison between the Military Ridge State Trail, Badger State Trail and, eventually, the Glacial Drumlin State Trail. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and in-line skating.

name: Devil’s River State Trail
notes: This scenic rail trail in Brown and Manitowoc counties travels through four small communities while passing by a wide variety of scenery, including farmlands, prairies, rivers and wetlands. No state trail pass required. See website for additional details.

name: Elroy-Sparta State Trail
notes: Considered the first rail-to-trail in the United States, the trail features three rock tunnels and five small towns along its 32.5-mile route. A state trail pass is required for bicycling. See website for additional details.

name: Fox River State Trail
notes: From downtown Green Bay, the Fox River Trail winds along the beautiful Fox River before extending for 25 miles south ending near the Town of Hilbert. A state trail pass is required for bicycling, in-line skating and horseback riding. Open 5am-9pm.

name: Gandy Dancer State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is required for bicycling for the southern segment, but not the northern.

name: Glacial Drumlin State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is required for bicycling and in-line skating. Running between Wisconsin's two largest urban areas, this trail stretches for 52 miles through farmlands and glacial topography.

name: Great Sauk State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is required for bicycling and in-line skating.

name: Green Circle State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is not required on the trail.

name: Hank Aaron State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is not required on the trail.

name: Military Ridge State Trail
notes: The 40-mile Military Ridge State Trail connects Dodgeville and Madison by way of an 1855 military route between Verona and Dodgeville. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and in-line skating. See website for additional details.

name: Mound View State Trail
notes: This pleasant, gently-rolling trail in southwest Wisconsin connects the communities of Platteville and Belmont. A state trail pass is not required on the trail. See website for additional details.

name: Mountain-Bay State Trail
notes: The Mountain-Bay State Trail is one of the longest rail-trails in Wisconsin. The trail travels for 83 miles between the two geologic features it is named for; Rib Mountain and Green Bay. A state trail pass is required for bicycling.

name: Newton Blackmour State Trail
notes: The Newton Blackmour State Trail spans 22 miles on a former rail corridor in Outagamie County. A state trail pass is not required on the trail.

name: Oconto River State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is not required on the trail. This 8-mile trail passes through the forests and farms of Oconto County between the communities of Oconto and Stiles Junction.

name: Stower Seven Lakes State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is required for bicycling and cross-country skiing.

name: Sugar River State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is required for bicycling.

name: Tomorrow River State Trail
notes: This 29-mile rail trail travels through scenic glacial terrain and farm country from Plover in Portage County to just outside the village of Manawa in Waupaca County. A state trail pass is required for bicycling and horseback riding.

name: Tuscobia State Trail
notes: This 74-mile trail on a former rail corridor is one of the longest rail trails in the state, running from Park Falls to the Wild Rivers State Trail just north of Rice Lake. A state trail pass is not required on the trail. See website for more details.

name: Wild Rivers State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is not required on the trail. The Wild Rivers State Trail stretches 104 miles through Douglas, Washburn and Barron counties in northwest Wisconsin. See website for additional details.

name: Wolf River State Trail
notes: A state trail pass is not required on the trail. The Wolf River State Trail runs 33 miles on a former rail corridor from White Lake to Crandon. See website for additional details.

name: Blackhawk Lake State Recreation Area
notes: Part of the park is closed seasonally. There are other parking areas outside of the closed section. Blackhawk Lake Wildlife Area is a 2,037-acre property in west-central Iowa County. See website for more details.

name: Willow Flowage State Wilderness Area
notes: 6am - 11pm. No vehicle sticker required. With limited development and access, the Willow Flowage Scenic Waters Area is a large, island-studded reservoir with a truly wild flavor.

name: Chippewa Flowage State Wilderness Area
notes: 6am - 11pm. No vehicle sticker required. The Chippewa Flowage, a 15,300-acre impoundment, dotted with about 200 undeveloped islands, it is Wisconsin's third-largest lake. See website for additional details.

name: Adell State Wildlife Area
notes: Parking at posted coordinates. Parking is right off of someones driveway, please only activate this park during the day. See website for more details.

name: Albany State Wildlife Area
notes: This property currently consists of 1,421-acres of state-owned land, 3 acres of easements and 282 acres of leased lands for public hunting, fishing, trapping and other nature-based activities. Check website for additional details.

name: Allenton Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Allenton Marsh Wildlife Area is a 1,160-acre property in western Washington County. Check website for additional details.

name: Avon Bottoms State Wildlife Area
notes: The property currently consists of 3,402 acres of fee-title state-owned lands and four acres of easement lands. Check website for additional details.

name: Big Swamp State Wildlife Area
notes: Big Swamp Wildlife Area is a 796-acre property in Buffalo County. Check website for additional details.

name: Bloomfield State Wildlife Area
notes: Bloomfield Wildlife Area is a 1,203-acre property located in southeastern Walworth County. Check website for additional details.

name: Brooklyn State Wildlife Area
notes: The property currently consists of 2,608 acres of state-owned land, 337 acres of easement and 151 acres of leased lands. Check website for additional details.

name: Buena Vista State Wildlife Area
notes: Buena Vista Wildlife Area is a 12,700-acre property located in southwestern Portage County. Buena Vista Wildlife Area consists of scattered parcels 10 miles east of Wisconsin Rapids and 4 miles south of Plover. Check website for additional details.

name: Buzz Besadny State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: 2,632-acre property located in Kewaunee County. Find it west of Kewaunee with many access points. Check website for additional details.

name: Colburn State Wildlife Area
notes: Colburn Wildlife Area is a 4,965 acre property located in north-central Adams County near the Waushara County border. Check website for additional details.

name: Deansville State Wildlife Area
notes: Deansville Wildlife Area is a 1,970-acre property consisting of upland grassland/agricultural land, mixed hardwood upland forest, open marshland and sedge meadow as well as shrub carr and brushy areas. Check website for additional details.

name: Dewey Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Dewey Marsh contains a large expanse of relatively undisturbed northern sedge meadow including smaller islands of tamarack and black spruce swamp, paper birch and white pine woods and ericaceous bog. Check website for additional details.

name: Evansville State Wildlife Area
notes: Evansville Wildlife Area is located south and east of the city of Evansville in Rock County. It currently contains 707-acres of state owned, 100 acres of easements and 40 acres of leased lands. Check website for additional details.

name: Footville State Wildlife Area
notes: Footville Wildlife Area currently consists of several small state-owned or eased scattered wildlife land parcels (529 acres) and over 8,500 acres of leased land. Check website for additional details.

name: Grassy Lake State Wildlife Area
notes: 695-acre property located in Columbia County. Check website for additional details.

name: Greenwood State Wildlife Area
notes: Greenwood Wildlife Area is located in west central Waushara County, 3 miles northeast of Coloma and 1 mile southeast of Hancock. Check website for additional details.

name: Hook Lake Bog - Grass Lake State Wildlife Area
notes: Hook Lake Bog-Grass Lake Wildlife Area is a 1,096-acre property located 4 miles south of Madison and McFarland in the town of Dunn in Dane County. Check website for additional details.

name: Jefferson Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Check website for additional details. Jefferson Marsh Wildlife Area consists of approximately 3,000 acres.

name: Jennings Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Jennings Creek Wildlife Area is a 530-acre property located in Columbia County. Check website for additional details.

name: Koshkonong State Wildlife Area
notes: Koshkonong Wildlife Area is a property of approximately 800 acres consisting of a high quality deep water marsh, which transitions into shrub carr and bottomland hardwoods. Check website for additional details.

name: Leola Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Leola Marsh Wildlife Area is an 1,860-acre property located 15 miles southeast of Wisconsin Rapids. Check website for additional details.

name: Liberty Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Liberty Creek Wildlife Area is in Albany and Brooklyn townships in east central Green County. The property consists of 563 acres of state-owned and 20 acres of leased land. Check website for additional details.

name: Lima Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Lima Marsh Wildlife Area is a 2,514-acre property comprised of 2,048 acres of state-owned land and 466 acres leased for public hunting. Check website for additional details.

name: Mud Lake State Wildlife Area
notes: The wildlife area includes a 160-acre refuge that is closed to all entry from Sept. 1- Nov. 30 except for deer hunting during the gun and muzzleloader seasons.

name: Namekagon Barrens State Wildlife Area
notes: The Namekagon Barrens Wildlife Area is a uniquely beautiful 6,446-acre property located in the northern part of Burnett and Washburn counties, consisting of two units separated by a few miles. Check website for additional details.

name: New Munster State Wildlife Area
notes: New Munster Wildlife Area is 1,226-acre property located in western Kenosha County. Check website for additional details.

name: Nichols Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: 612-acre property located in the southwest portion of Sheboygan County. Check website for additional details. Cedar Lane Road is not seasonally maintained.

name: Outagamie State Wildlife Area
notes: Outagamie Wildlife Area is found in northwest Outagamie County and is around 1,000 acres. Check website for additional details.

name: Paradise Marsh State Wildlife Area
notes: Paradise Marsh Wildlife Area is a 1,588-acre property located in Columbia County. Check website for additional details.

name: Paradise Valley State Wildlife Area

notes: Activities: Hunting and Nature Viewing. Open 4 a.m.–9 p.m. Please review website and flyer for important details. A valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required.

name: Andrick Ponds State Wildlife Area
notes: Activities: Hunting and Nature Viewing. Open 4 a.m.–9 p.m., Sat., Sun., Wed. and state and federal holidays only. Please review website and flyer for important details. A valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required.

name: Russell Lakes State Wildlife Area
notes: Activities: Hunting, Wildlife Viewing. Public access prohibited Feb 15 thru Jul 15. Parking only in established parking areas. Camping during waterfowl hunting seasons by licensed hunters only. Valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required.

name: Alien Run Mountain Bike Trail BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: Fees None. No potable water, ADA-accessible vault toilet present. large, gravel parking area, two accessible, shaded picnic tables and a changing pavilion. Open year-round. The road may become difficult to navigate in bad weather. Unknown cell service.

name: Sunset Reef Campground BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: Reclaimed well pad, 11 developed campsites; five RV spaces and six tent sites. Sites has a shaded picnic table, fire pit and grill. dry camping for a maximum of five nights for free. No fees. One vault toilet, no potable water. Cell service available.

name: Parks Ranch Cave BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: No Fees. No restrooms or potable water. Primitive camping locations with fire rings. One shade shelter. Open year round. Be alert for rattlesnakes and other animals. sudden storms. subject to extreme flash flooding. Cell service available.

name: Glade Run Recreation Area BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: No Fees. Vault Toilet. No Potable water. large gravel parking lot. Brown Springs Campground/OHV Area, part of Glade Run. Camping, One group shelter. gas, food, water is in Farmington. Road may become impassable in bad weather. Camping permit required.

name: Hackmatack National Wildlife Refuge
notes: As with all NWRs, this site is very sensitive to any/all contact, and may have seasonal restrictions. Please check website and any appropriate ranger stations if there is any doubt about access.

name: Wood County State Wildlife Area
notes: Wood County Wildlife Area is a 21,000-acre property in southwestern Wood County, Wisconsin. The area features wetlands, forested uplands, and islands. See park website for more information and maps.

name: Waupaca River State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: Located in the Town of Farmington in Waupaca County, the Waupaca River Fishery Area consists of several scattered parcels totaling approximately 162 acres along the Waupaca River. See website for more info and maps.

name: Whitcomb Creek State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: The Whitcomb Creek Fishery Area is located in the Forest Transition Ecological Landscape of northwest Waupaca County. A few different parcels of land are available. See website for more details and maps.

name: Nicholson Ford Wildlife Area
notes: Wildlife area near the Iowa River. Note that the OHV park is adjacent but it is not a part of the Wildlife Area and is managed by a club. As such the OHV park does not qualify for POTA. You must hike or boat into the POTA entity.

name: Rice Lake State Fish and Wildlife Area
Upper Missouri River BLM Wild and Scenic River
notes: Activation must be within 100' of the Missouri River on the 149 miles section between Fort Benton and James Kipp Recreation Area. Please do not log this park if you are upstream or downstream from this "BLM Wild and Scenic" portion of the river.

name: Axolotl Lakes BLM Wilderness Area
notes: To activate this entity will require a walk from the cabin or Day Use area, both of those areas or on BLM land but not within the boundary of this park, Axolotl Lakes Wilderness Study Area.

name: David Davis Mansion State Historic Site
Tamarack Creek State Wildlife Area
notes: Tamarack Creek Wildlife Area is a 542-acre property in Trempealeau County. See website for more details and maps of the area.

name: Canyon Ferry Wildlife Management Area
notes: This POTA entity is located just north of Townsend, the WMA does encompass the entire shore of Canyon Ferry Lake. Please see PDF map on webpage.

name: Fresno Reservoir Wildlife Management Area
notes: This POTA entity is located NE of the actual reservoir. This WMA does encompass the Bur Of Reclamation land on most of the shore of Fresno Reservoir. Please see PDF map on webpage or use your land ownership maps/apps.

name: Kootenai West Wildlife Management Area
notes: Please pay very special attention to access instructions on the website, this will help avoid private property and conflicts. Tread Lightly.

name: Kootenai Woods Ranch Wildlife Management Area

Huron Flats Wildlife Area
notes: Wildlife area near Mississippi River

name: Ocoee River State Park
notes: This park appears to consist of 8 discrete sites along the river. It does not appear to be a 2-fer with Cherokee National Forest as these recreation sites do not appear on the NFS maps for the Forest.

name: Red Rock Landing State Conservation Area
Seventy Six State Conservation Area
notes: There is a tract of private land inside this park, so make sure you know where you are.

name: Lesterville Access State Conservation Area
notes: Please be mindful of primary users at busy or peak periods. This is a small park with limited parking.

name: Reiker Ford Access State Conservation Area

name: Union Access State Conservation Area
notes: This is a very small park. Be mindful of primary users during peak or busy periods.

name: James Clark Access State Conservation Area

name: Long Wildlife Management Area
notes: Small undeveloped forest area. A small parking area is not completely within the boundary - so realistically, to activate this one, you and all of your equipment will need to cross the fence to be in the park.

name: Gunnison State Wildlife Area
notes: Activities: Hunting, Fishing, Archery & Nature Viewing. Closed Dec 1st to Apr 30th. A valid hunting or fishing license OR SWA pass is required.

name: Gunnison River State Wildlife Area

name: Indian Nations National Wildlife Area

name: Mallard Marsh:Gombold Unit Wildlife Management Area
East Phillips Canyon Wildlife Management Area
notes: The access road is not well maintained. Low maintenance county road. The road leads through a cut in the surrounding hills. It could drift closed in the winter with snow. Road shows signs of washing out. 4x4 recommended or hiking into the site.

name: Sibley Wildlife Management Area
notes: Verified with park ranger that this is NOT part of state park

name: Sigler Wildlife Management Area
notes: See park notes for waterfowl season road openings/closings

name: Mount Jumbo Wildlife Management Area

name: North Swan Valley Wildlife Management Area
notes: These boundaries are tricky, the WMA is checkerboarded with nearby Flathead National Forest and Swan River State Forest. These are not 2'fers or 3'fers. Please reference land ownership maps to make sure you are activating the park you think you are.

name: Roundhorn Wildlife Management Area
notes: Very small WMA, 27 acres. Please tread lightly.

name: MT Fish Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: This park is not a 2'fer with Fish Creek State Park, they are both owned by the state of Montana but do not share the same footprint. Please refer to your land ownership maps to know which entity you are on prior to activation.

name: West Salt Creek Wildlife Area
notes: Rural Wildlife Area with a gravel parking lot.

name: Bear River Divide State HMA Wildlife Area

name: Logan Cave National Wildlife Refuge

name: Pastorius Reservoir State Wildlife Area

name: Canyon Creek Wildlife Management Area
notes: Open May 15 to Nov 30

name: Head of the Crow State Park

name: Newton Lakes BOR Recreation Site
notes: Picnic tables, restrooms, boat ramp. See also: https://www.usbr.gov/gp/recreation/bbrrec3.html

name: Ralston Reservoir BOR & State Fish and Wildlife Area
notes: No fishing. Excellent wildlife viewing area, especially wetland and waterfowl species (ducks, pelicans, and sandhill cranes). Available services include accessible bridge and walkway to viewing area. No restroom. No overnight camping. No drinking water.

name: Miles Landing BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: Miles Landing is a day-use area, popular for picnicking, bank fishing and boating. There are picnic tables with shade structures, a boat ramp, and a vault toilet. The area is ADA accessible.

name: Wheatland Reservoir #3 BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: Wheatland Reservoir #3 features a boat ramp, ample parking, and several restroom facilities. Activate only in the parking and boat ramp area.

name: Whitetail Day Use BLM Recreation Management Area
notes: Boat ramp, parking area, interpretive signs and a vault toilet. It is ADA accessible.

name: Prospect Mountain WSA State Wilderness Area
notes: From Riverside WY, take WY 230E for 19 miles to Prospect Peak road and turn left. Travel about five miles and park on the side of the road and hike in.

name: Sweetwater Rocks (Lankin Dome) State Wilderness Area
notes: Motorized travel is expressly prohibited. Additionally, the WSA is closed to mineral entry, including gold panning.

name: Camp Creek State Wildlife Habitat Management Area
notes: NOT a 2-fer with the adjacent Bridger-Teton National Forest. Be alert, this is bear country!

name: Patrol Cabin State Wildlife Habitat Management Area
notes: The WHMA is located 24 miles northeast of Jackson, WY. Vehicular access is available via the Upper Gros Ventre road and sits adjacent to Breakneck Flat - Cottonwood Creek road. The elk feedground can be visited by oversnow vehicles during winter months.

name: Fall Creek State Wildlife Habitat Management Area
notes: This WHMA lies within bear country. It is six miles southeast of Pinedale, WY.

name: Dubois Badlands BLM Wilderness Area
notes: You will need to use your navigational skills to access the Dubois Badlands WSA from the Dubois dump road.

name: Adobe Town BLM Wilderness Area
notes: Access to wild lands inherently requires good navigational skills and four-wheel drive or high-clearance vehicles. Be prepared for adverse weather and road conditions. Area is restricted and does not allow for the use of motorized and mechanized equipment

name: Pryor Mountain BLM Wilderness Area
notes: See the website for access instructions. Approximately nine miles south of Lovell, WY

name: Sheep Mountain BLM Wilderness Area
